title: The project you are standing in
summary: Composer, PSR-4, the public document root, and tests you write yourself.

blocks.html: Everything so far ran as a single file. The repository around this course is a small Composer project, and every piece of it exists for a reason we have already met: classes live in src/, the pages live in public/, and one generated file, vendor/autoload.php, knows where every class is so no page ever writes a require for GradeCalculator.

blocks.title: the repository
blocks.ascii:
php-basic/
  composer.json      the name, the PHP version, the PSR-4 map
  composer.lock      exact versions, committed
  Makefile           up / shell / lint / test
  docker-compose.yml the PHP 8.4 + Apache services
  src/
    GradeCalculator.php    App\GradeCalculator
  public/            <- the document root
    index.php              entry point
    atm_withdrawal.php
    gradeCalculator.index.php
    example.php
    student_directory_with_functions_array.php
  vendor/
    autoload.php     generated from composer.json
  usr/config/
    php.ini          display_errors off, production
    php.ini-dev      display_errors on, development

blocks.html: Apache's document root is public/, so a URL maps to a file in there and nowhere else: /gradeCalculator.index.php is that file. public/index.php is the front page, and it pulls in one exercise at a time with include — the line that is commented out is the one that is not running.

Never point the document root at the repository root. A .php file in the web root gets executed, which is what you want, but composer.json, composer.lock, .env, and anything in vendor/ would then be served as plain text to anyone who guesses the path. public/ is the only directory the world may see.

blocks.title: a page uses the class
blocks.code:
<?php

use App\GradeCalculator;

$calculator = new GradeCalculator(
    quiz: 90.0,
    assignment: 88.0,
    midterm: 91.5,
    final: 87.0,
);

echo number_format($calculator->getFinalGrade(), 2), "\n";
echo $calculator->getLetterGrade(), "\n";
echo $calculator->getRemarks(), "\n";
echo $calculator->isPassed() ? 'passed' : 'failed', "\n";

blocks.html: There is no require line for the class, and the file is never named. composer.json holds the map: "App\\": "src/" means the namespace App lives in src/. PSR-4 means the rest of the class name is the path, so App\GradeCalculator is src/GradeCalculator.php, and that file opens with namespace App; while the page that uses it writes use App\GradeCalculator;. vendor/autoload.php is Composer's register-on-demand loader built from that map; composer dump-autoload rebuilds it after you add a class, and public/index.php requires it once for every page.

blocks.title: declare(strict_types=1) at the top
blocks.code:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use App\GradeCalculator;

try {
    new GradeCalculator(quiz: "90", assignment: 80.0, midterm: 80.0, final: 80.0);
    echo "the string was accepted\n";
} catch (TypeError $e) {
    echo 'rejected with ', get_class($e), "\n";
}

blocks.html:
declare(strict_types=1); must be the first statement in the file and it applies to the file it is written in. With it, a string handed to a float parameter is a TypeError; without it the same call quietly converts "90" to 90.0 and the bug moves to the report. src/GradeCalculator.php declares it, and every page that calls into it should too.

Above the classes, composer.json requires php: ^8.4 and defines two scripts: lint runs php -l over every file, test is the hook where a test framework goes. The Makefile wraps the daily commands — make up starts the containers, make shell opens a shell inside the PHP container, make lint lints everything the container can see.

blocks.title: tests without a framework
blocks.code:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use App\GradeCalculator;

function assertEquals(string $label, string $expected, string $actual): void
{
    if ($actual !== $expected) {
        throw new RuntimeException($label . ': expected ' . $expected . ', got ' . $actual);
    }

    echo 'ok  ', $label, "\n";
}

$good = new GradeCalculator(quiz: 90.0, assignment: 88.0, midterm: 91.5, final: 87.0);
$poor = new GradeCalculator(quiz: 50.0, assignment: 50.0, midterm: 50.0, final: 50.0);

assertEquals('letter for 88.93', 'B+', $good->getLetterGrade());
assertEquals('fifty percent fails', 'failed', $poor->isPassed() ? 'passed' : 'failed');

echo "2 passed\n";
blocks.output:
ok  letter for 88.93
ok  fifty percent fails
2 passed

blocks.title: and one that fails
blocks.code:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use App\GradeCalculator;

function assertEquals(string $label, string $expected, string $actual): void
{
    if ($actual !== $expected) {
        throw new RuntimeException($label . ': expected ' . $expected . ', got ' . $actual);
    }
}

try {
    $good = new GradeCalculator(quiz: 90.0, assignment: 88.0, midterm: 91.5, final: 87.0);
    assertEquals('letter for 88.93', 'A', $good->getLetterGrade());
    echo "everything passed\n";
} catch (RuntimeException $e) {
    echo 'failed: ', $e->getMessage(), "\n";
}
blocks.output: failed: letter for 88.93: expected A, got B+

blocks.html: That is the whole idea of a test runner: a list of expected-versus-actual pairs, each one throwing on a mismatch. make test is where PHPUnit goes — the test script in composer.json already points at phpunit, and the Makefile target currently just prints a reminder. When the suite grows past a screenful, that is the moment to install it.

Where to go next. Open the four exercise pages and read them top to bottom; you can now read every line of them.

  • public/atm_withdrawal.php — a PIN check with a session-held balance and form validation.
  • public/gradeCalculator.index.php — the form that feeds App\GradeCalculator, including the match in getRemarks().
  • public/student_directory_with_functions_array.php — arrays, loops, and functions doing the work.
  • public/example.php — array functions and objects side by side.

Then read the three manual pages linked below this chapter — autoloading, namespaces, and type declarations — and the language reference they sit in. Change one number in src/GradeCalculator.php, refresh, and watch the page follow the code. That loop — edit, run, read the output — is the whole job.

quiz.q: Which directory should Apache serve as the document root?
quiz.why: public/ holds the pages and nothing else. Anything outside it — composer.json, .env, src/, vendor/ — then has no URL and cannot be downloaded.

quiz.q: With PSR-4 "App\\": "src/", where must App\GradeCalculator live?
quiz.why: The prefix App\ is mapped to src/, and the remaining class name is the path: GradeCalculator.php. The filename must match the class name exactly, case included.

quiz.q: What does declare(strict_types=1) change about a call to a function with typed parameters?
options: It makes argument checks strict in that file, so a string is not silently cast to float
It makes the whole project strict for every file
quiz.why: It applies per file and is checked at the call site: with it, a string passed to a float parameter throws TypeError instead of being converted.

exercise.brief: Build a GradeCalculator for quiz 90, assignment 88, midterm 91.5, and final 87, then print its letter grade on the first line and passed or failed on the second. The class comes from App, so add use App\GradeCalculator; at the top.
exercise.starter:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use App\GradeCalculator;

// 1. build a calculator with quiz 90.0, assignment 88.0, midterm 91.5, final 87.0
// 2. print its letter grade
// 3. print passed or failed, using isPassed()
exercise.hint: Named arguments keep the four scores readable: new GradeCalculator(quiz: 90.0, assignment: 88.0, midterm: 91.5, final: 87.0). For the second line a ternary is enough: $calculator->isPassed() ? 'passed' : 'failed'.
exercise.solution:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use App\GradeCalculator;

$calculator = new GradeCalculator(
    quiz: 90.0,
    assignment: 88.0,
    midterm: 91.5,
    final: 87.0,
);

echo $calculator->getLetterGrade(), "\n";
echo $calculator->isPassed() ? 'passed' : 'failed', "\n";
